data.narrative:
Exowatt, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Hannan Happi and Jack Abraham, has raised $90M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comparison set of 9 peers across the Climate & Energy sector—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private entities including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within narrow valuation tiers; a full-sector median would lack precision.

The Stage-Progression method forms the primary basis for valuation. Using the $90M total raised as a proxy for enterprise value and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier at Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $180M. This represents the quantifiable result from the single applicable triangulation method.

The analysis supports a range of $153M (low) to $207M (high), with $180M as the central estimate. Key uncertainties stem from the limited peer dataset—the method relies on a single scaling assumption rather than market-derived comparables—and the absence of sufficient same-stage or tier-matched private transactions in the sector. Refinement would benefit from additional Series A or Series B transaction data within climate hardware and energy storage.
